excerpt: Noise can feel like drowning. This is often intentional and a large part of its appeal to the sickos, but even the largest of whales comes up for air every 15 minutes—breaking the surface tension, pupils constricting toward the atmosphere, and taking a bus-sized gulp. Is there anything that experimental noise can learn from this mammalian constraint? Max Klebanoff is working on it.
